modern: He who does not have one and always the same aim in life cannot be one and the same all through his life. But what I have said is not enough, unless this is added too: what this aim ought to be. For just as there is not the same opinion about all the things which the majority consider good in one way or another, but only about certain things, that is, things which concern the common interest, so too we ought to set before ourselves an aim which is social and political. For he who directs all his own efforts to this aim will make all his acts alike, and so will always be the same.
original: He who has not one and always the same object in life, cannot be one and the same all through his life. But what I have said is not enough, unless this also is added, what this object ought to be. For as there is not the same opinion about all the things which in some way or other are considered by the majority to be good, but only about some certain things, that is, things which concern the common interest, so also ought we to propose to ourselves an object which shall be of a common kind [social] and political. For he who directs all his own efforts to this object, will make all his acts alike, and thus will always be the same.

explained.summary: If you don’t have one consistent aim, you can’t be one consistent person. But any aim won’t do. People disagree about most things they call good, yet agree on what benefits everyone, so your aim should be the common good. Direct everything towards that and your actions will hang together, and you’ll be the same person all through.
explained.today: Without a steady aim it’s easy to be one person at work, another with your family and another online, pulled around by whatever’s in front of you. Asking whether something helps the people around you gives a single thread to run through all three.
